result: The authors reconstructed a whole-body connectome from a 3-day-old Platynereis larva using serial EM, identifying 9162 cells with somas and tracing 5.66 million nodes with ~28,000 pre- and postsynaptic sites, though ~15-19% of synaptic sites remained on unattached fragments.
evaluation: Reviewers describe this as 'an exceptional, high-quality and detailed description' and 'a wealth of high-quality data.' The reconstruction is characterized as 'painstakingly meticulous,' with no concerns raised about the completeness or quality of the dataset despite the presence of unattached fragments.

result: The Platynereis larval nervous system comprises an anterior brain connected to a paired ventral nerve cord (VNC) via circumesophageal connectives, with the trunk organized into five segments. Sensory neurons project ipsilaterally to ventro-lateral VNC bundles, interneurons have ipsi- or contralateral projections within the VNC neuropil, and motoneurons uniquely have peripheral projections with motor nerves concentrating dorsally.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the work provides detailed anatomical descriptions and organization of the nervous system. The anatomical claims are part of the 'massive amount of high-quality data' that reviewers found convincing, with no specific critiques of these structural descriptions.

result: Neurons exhibit diverse morphological properties: median cable length of 97.1 µm (ranging to 1.2-1.7 mm for the largest neurons), median of 8 presynaptic and 6 postsynaptic sites (with largest neurons having >300 presynapses), and the ratio of pre- to postsynaptic sites distinguishes neuron classes. Most neurons are unipolar with <100 segments and lack primary cilia, though sensory neurons are bipolar with 0-5 sensory cilia.
evaluation: These morphological characterizations are part of the 'painstakingly meticulous' analysis praised by reviewers. The quantitative data and morphological descriptions are included in the 'wealth of data' that reviewers found to be of high quality, with no concerns raised about these measurements.

result: The synaptic connectome contains 2675 nodes connected by 14,066 directed edges formed by 26,881 synapses, forming a sparsely connected network (density 0.00197). Source nodes are predominantly sensory neurons, sink nodes are mostly effector cells, and the highest-degree nodes include ciliomotor neurons (Loop, Ser-tr1), sensory-motoneuron pygPBunp, and MNspinning.
evaluation: Reviewers describe the network analysis as part of the 'massive amount of high-quality data' and note the work provides detailed information about 'how sensory neurons, interneurons, motor neurons, and effector organs are connected.' No concerns were raised about the network statistics or connectivity patterns.

result: Community detection using the Leiden algorithm identified several functional modules in the connectome, including the anterior neurosecretory centre, mushroom bodies, visual circuit, ciliomotor network, mechanosensory modules, postural control module, and muscle-motor modules. Nodes within modules are more strongly interconnected than between modules, and several modules contain neurons previously shown to mediate specific behaviors.
evaluation: Reviewers note the work 'provides a wealth of data on cell type diversity and the modules that interconnect them' and will be useful for 'studies on cell type diversity, segmental vs. intersegmental connectivity, and mushroom bodies.' The modular organization is part of the accepted high-quality analysis.

result: The authors classified 966 neurons into 202 cell types (most represented by only 2 cells) and 3128 non-neuronal cells into 92 types, including diverse cell types such as epidermal, pigment, muscle, ciliated, glial, and gland cells. Developing structures (antennae, palps, stomodeum) contain immature sensory neurons with few synapses.
evaluation: Reviewers emphasize this work 'lays the foundations for studies on cell type diversity' and note the 'painstakingly meticulous' analysis. The comprehensive cell type classification is central to the paper's contribution and was not questioned by reviewers.

result: The cell-type connectome includes 84 sensory, 82 interneuron, 34 motoneuron, and 58 effector cell types, connected by 2410 edges formed by 14,640 synapses. Left-right connectivity shows high stereotypy (correlation 0.91), and network parameters are similar to C. elegans and C. intestinalis connectomes.
evaluation: Reviewers note this is 'only the third whole body connectome to be assembled' and provides 'a comparison with those less complex animals: the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans and the tunicate Ciona intestinalis.' The comparative analysis and stereotypy findings are accepted without critique.

result: Circuit analysis identified 4 sensory-motor neurons with direct motor output, 25 premotor sensory neurons, and a maximum of 5 hops from sensory neurons to effectors. 33 sensory neurons have no synaptic paths to effectors, of which 19 are neurosecretory cells with few synaptic partners.
evaluation: These circuit organization findings are part of the detailed connectivity analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The identification of different circuit motifs and path lengths contributes to understanding 'unimodal and multimodal sensory processing, and long-range and short-range connectivity' that reviewers noted.

result: Neurotransmitters or neuropeptides were assigned to 53 (26%) neuronal cell types, including 11 cholinergic, 3 serotonergic, 1 dopaminergic, 1 adrenergic, and 4 glutamatergic types, plus 38 cell types expressing one of 12 neuropeptides. 516 connectome neurons contained dense core vesicles indicative of peptidergic transmission.
evaluation: The molecular characterization is part of the comprehensive dataset that reviewers praised. While reviewers note the paper is 'burdensome to read and understand' due to its size, they do not question the validity of the molecular annotations provided.

result: The head contains 45 sensory neuron types and 52 head interneuron types, with information flowing from sensory clusters through interneurons to ciliomotor neurons, ventral motoneurons (vMNs), and descending interneurons. The vMNs form a postural control module that innervates contralateral muscles and ciliated cells. Several ciliomotor neurons directly innervate locomotor ciliary bands, and visual photoreceptors share postsynaptic interneurons with eyespot photoreceptors.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the work provides detailed circuit-level analysis and will be useful to 'scientists interested in other nervous systems parts, their functions, and evolution.' The head circuit organization is part of the accepted high-quality data, with no specific concerns raised.

result: The mushroom bodies (MBs) comprise ventrolateral brain ganglia with sensory neurons (SNMB) and interneurons (INMB) classified into intrinsic and output projection types. MBs receive input from MB-intrinsic sensory neurons, antennae, palps, and other sensory types, with cell-type-specific connectivity organized into micro-circuits. The MB architecture is multilayer, parallel, and feed-forward with weak recurrent connections, showing left-right symmetry (correlation 0.76) and a fan-out fan-in organization that may support associative memory formation.
evaluation: Reviewers specifically note this work 'lays the foundations for studies on...mushroom bodies' and will be useful for scientists interested in these structures. The detailed MB analysis is part of the comprehensive dataset praised by reviewers, though one reviewer suggested 'there could be a single paper on the mushroom body' due to the depth of analysis.

result: Brain-trunk connectivity involves 138 descending brain neurons and 75 ascending VNC neurons, with 549 trunk cells receiving synapses from head neurons and 288 head cells receiving synapses from trunk neurons. Trunk-projecting brain neurons have either decussating or ipsilaterally descending morphology, projecting to different VNC domains with different targets, and receive most inputs in the central head neuropil while forming most presynapses in the VNC.
evaluation: This analysis of brain-trunk connectivity is part of the 'long-range and short-range connectivity' that reviewers noted the paper extracts. The detailed characterization of descending and ascending pathways is included in the accepted high-quality dataset.

result: The trunk comprises three chaetigerous segments plus a cryptic segment and pygidium, with ciliary bands marking segment boundaries. Connectivity analysis shows strongest connections within segments but also inter-segmental connections (except segment 0). Segment 1 interneurons connect to four other body regions, and the head, segment 1, and pygidium contain neurons with 'global reach' projecting along the entire body length. Different effector types receive innervation from specific segments.
evaluation: Reviewers note the work 'lays the foundations for studies on...segmental vs. intersegmental connectivity' and 'informs the understanding of the evolution of segmental body plans in annelids.' The segmental organization analysis is a key contribution that reviewers found valuable, though one suggested it could be a separate paper.

result: Segment-specific neuronal cell types include 10 in segment 1 (including ciliomotor neurons for body-wide ciliary control), 8 in segment 2 (including giant MNspinning motoneurons innervating contralateral spinning glands and forming reciprocal connections with INsplit interneurons), 2 in segment 3, and 7 in the pygidium (including motoneurons innervating head pigment cells). Several neuron types (chaeMech, INsplitPB, INbackcross, MNche, MNhose) occur in all chaetigerous segments.
evaluation: The detailed segment-specific cell type analysis is part of the comprehensive characterization that reviewers praised. This contributes to understanding 'the evolution of segmental body plans in annelids' that reviewers noted as a key finding.

result: Four cell-type families (CR, PU, PB, INsplit) and two muscle types (MUSlongV, MUStrans) occur across five or six body regions (head, segments 0-3, pygidium), a pattern that may indicate serial homology and suggest a metameric evolutionary origin for trunk segments, pygidium, and head.
evaluation: Reviewers note the work draws 'several interesting conclusions' including insights about evolution, specifically that 'circuit evolution might have proceeded by duplication and diversion of cell types.' This evolutionary inference from cell type distribution patterns is accepted as part of the paper's contributions.

result: Mechanosensory neurons and their postsynaptic partners form an anatomically distinct 'mechanosensory girdle' spanning the entire body, including penetrating collar receptor (CR), biciliated (PB), uniciliated (PU), and interparapodial multiciliated (interparaPM) neurons, all with penetrating sensory cilia surrounded by microvilli. CR and PB neurons express mechanosensory polycystins PKD2-1 (and PKD1-1 for CRs). The girdle also includes chaeMech dendritic cells that are chaetal mechanoreceptors.
evaluation: This identification of a body-wide mechanosensory system is part of the detailed circuit analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The mechanosensory girdle represents a novel organizational principle that contributes to understanding nervous system organization.

result: The chaeMech cells are dendritic sensory cells in segments 1-3 with dendrites branching between chaetal sacs, potentially sensing chaetal displacement during crawling (proprioception) or external stimuli. They are highly interconnected and project to the VNC where they synapse on premotor interneurons (INsplitCR, INsplitBronto, INchaeMech) and motoneurons (MNring, MNspinning). Their innervation of MNspinning suggests mechanosensation may regulate glandular secretion. The postsynaptic circuits of CRs and chaeMechs are only partially overlapping, with shared innervation of INsplitCR suggesting proprioceptive feedback during startle responses.
evaluation: The detailed analysis of chaeMech connectivity and function is part of the comprehensive circuit characterization that reviewers praised. The functional inferences about proprioception and feedback are supported by the connectivity data and comparative references, fitting within the accepted analytical framework.

result: The strongest postsynaptic partners of girdle mechanosensory neurons are ipsilateral INsplit interneurons with bifurcating projections, subdivided into distinct cell types (INsplitCR, INsplitPB, INsplitPBant, INsplitPB-RF/Ya, INsplitPUh, INsplitBronto, INCM) occurring in all four trunk segments and head with unique synaptic connectivity. Different mechanosensory types specifically target different INsplit subtypes. INsplitCR and INsplitPB are highly ranked by connectivity, suggesting integrating functions. INsplit neurons are premotor, connecting to trunk motoneurons that innervate glands, ciliated cells, muscles, and pigment cells, thus mechanosensory neurons provide input to all effector systems.
evaluation: This detailed characterization of the INsplit interneuron family and their role in mechanosensory processing is part of the comprehensive circuit analysis that reviewers found to be of high quality. The identification of cell-type-specific connectivity patterns contributes to understanding sensory processing organization.
